method: Every settled image, of either arm, whose only fault is lettering and whose scorers called some of it readable. The operator classified each by its blind id from both scorers' and the adjudicators' notes, without looking up its arm. Lettering-only images the scorers agreed held no readable writing are accepted without a ruling. The strict scores are unchanged.

items.basis: A white question mark painted in the air above a figure: a caption-like symbol, not a mark on an object.
A playing-card corner index ('5') and pips.
Digit strings in a newspaper headline row; no word.
A newspaper masthead that reads roughly as the word 'Banner'.
Block capitals on newspapers that spell no word.
The readable word 'Missing' heads the slip.
A playing-card corner index ('A') and pips.
Carved capitals on a milestone that spell no word ('RONAN / AILETE').
A milestone reading 'DANASUS', which a reader takes for the place name Damascus.
Carved pseudo-Latin on a milestone ('MIM / III'); not words in the reader's language.
A signature-like scrawl in the bottom-right corner.
Capitals on a tin label that spell no word.
